note: A flight attendant who until the day before this call was also working part-time in property management is not a business owner, physician or equivalent, and the income criterion fails outright and explicitly: 'I just, I can't justify 6k, especially in my current financial situation', he considered $600 over three months expensive, he has needed two jobs to get by, and Klarna declined him twice on a soft check. On starting point he is closer to rescue than to good-to-great — 198 lb against a best of 175, belly fat he says he has never been able to lose in 34 years, waking 'like I've gotten hit by a bus'. He does match on the other two and matches them genuinely: health is the area squeezed out by a punishing roster and two jobs, and he is emphatically not gym-averse — he owns kettlebells, has more on order, trained all last week, and once lost 60 to 70 lb under his own steam. The contrast with the Luis Ortiz call on the same day is the useful finding: both sit outside the stated ICP on the same three criteria, one closed on a split payment and one did not, and the difference was liquidity rather than fit. That supports the existing observation that income screening is filtering on a constraint the payment plan is supposed to solve — except here the payment plan could not solve it, because the only monthly route costs $1,800 more.
